input.message: What wavelength ranges do the six SPHEREx detector bands cover?

expected.behavior: Distinguish the six detector ranges from individual narrow bandpasses and the 102 cube channels. Give nominal R values with the IRSA source; no observation-data tool is needed.
expected.reference_answer: IRSA lists these detector ranges in microns, with nominal resolving power R: band 1 0.75-1.09 (39), band 2 1.10-1.62 (41), band 3 1.63-2.41 (41), band 4 2.42-3.82 (35), band 5 3.83-4.41 (112), band 6 4.42-5.00 (128). A detector band contains many pixel-dependent narrow bandpasses, not one uniform wavelength.

input.message: What is a brown dwarf?

expected.behavior: Define lack of sustained ordinary hydrogen fusion; do not rule out temporary deuterium fusion. Name the source; no observation-data tool is needed.
expected.reference_answer: A brown dwarf is a substellar object that cannot sustain ordinary hydrogen fusion like a main-sequence star. Sufficiently massive brown dwarfs can briefly fuse deuterium, so saying they never undergo any fusion is inaccurate. Sources: NASA Gliese 229 image description and JPL, A Cosmic Identity Crisis.

expected.reference_answer: Kahverengi cüce, ana kol yıldızı gibi sıradan hidrojen füzyonunu sürdüremeyen yıldız altı bir cisimdir. Yeterince büyük kütleli olanları kısa süre döteryum füzyonu yapabilir; hiçbir tür füzyon yapmadıklarını söylemek doğru değildir. Kaynaklar: NASA Gliese 229 görsel açıklaması ve JPL, A Cosmic Identity Crisis.

input.message: What does the H-R diagram plot?

expected.behavior: Distinguish luminosity or absolute magnitude from apparent brightness and give the conventional temperature-axis direction. Name the source; no observation-data tool is needed.
expected.reference_answer: The H-R diagram plots stellar luminosity or absolute magnitude against effective surface temperature or spectral type. Temperature conventionally decreases to the right. Apparent brightness alone is not intrinsic luminosity. Source: Chandra educational material on the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram.

input.message: What are Y dwarfs?

expected.behavior: Explain the cool spectral class; mentioning the WISE discovery context is welcome but optional (team decision 2026-11-14). Do not repeat a historical object count as current or use temperature alone as a definitive class. Name the source.
expected.reference_answer: Y dwarfs are the coolest spectral class of brown dwarfs, with effective temperatures typically below about 500 K. WISE data led to the first spectroscopically confirmed examples in 2011. Their class is based on spectral properties, not temperature alone. Source: CfA, Y-Type Stars; the article is historical, not a current object census.

input.message: Is the pixel value in a SPHEREx image the flux of the star?

expected.behavior: Distinguish MJy/sr surface brightness from integrated flux density and explain the need for background and photometry corrections. No observation-data tool is needed.
expected.reference_answer: No. The SPHEREx Level 2 IMAGE layer contains surface brightness in MJy/sr, not the integrated flux density of a star. Flux extraction requires background subtraction and aperture or PSF photometry, including the relevant solid-angle conversion and corrections. Source: IRSA Spectral Image documentation.

expected.reference_answer: Hayır. SPHEREx Level 2 IMAGE katmanı yıldızın toplam akı yoğunluğunu değil, MJy/sr cinsinden yüzey parlaklığını içerir. Akı ölçümü; arka plan çıkarımı, açıklık veya PSF fotometrisi, uygun katı açı dönüşümü ve gerekli düzeltmeleri gerektirir. Kaynak: IRSA Tayfsal Görüntü belgeleri.

input.message: How do SPHEREx cutouts work?

expected.behavior: Explain spatial subsetting with preserved coordinate and wavelength mappings. A cutout does not add temporal or spectral coverage; check release-specific PSF guidance. Name the source.
expected.reference_answer: A cutout is a spatial subset of an existing spectral image, not a new observation or a full spectrum. IRSA accepts a center and size on a returned image URL and updates the spatial and wavelength mapping. Check the product release, uncertainty, quality flags and applicable PSF. Source: IRSA SPHEREx data access documentation.

input.message: What is the mass range of brown dwarfs?

expected.behavior: Attribute the approximate ranges to their sources, distinguish deuterium and sustained-hydrogen boundaries, and explain that formation-based nomenclature may differ. Do not equate every historical range difference with two proven competing definitions.
expected.reference_answer: A common mass-based convention is about 13-80 Jupiter masses: deuterium burning sets the lower boundary and sustained hydrogen burning the upper one. Gan et al. (2025) describe this convention. Older NASA StarChild material gives 15-75 and JPL (2003) gives 10-70. These are approximate conventions, not universal exact limits; formation-based terminology can differ. Sources: the three linked references.

expected.reference_answer: Kütleye dayalı yaygın bir tanım yaklaşık 13-80 Jüpiter kütlesidir: alt sınır döteryum, üst sınır sürekli hidrojen yakımıyla ilişkilidir. Gan ve arkadaşları (2025) bu tanımı kullanır. Eski NASA StarChild metni 15-75, JPL (2003) ise 10-70 verir. Bunlar kesin evrensel sınırlar değildir; oluşum biçimine dayalı adlandırma farklılaşabilir. Kaynaklar: bağlantılı üç referans.
